Question: Give me a scientist who authored 100 scientific articles or more.

human: Useful: scientists are humans (domain restriction for the answer variable)

scientist_occupation: Useful: Wikidata item for the occupation 'scientist' (used with P106 occupation)

scholarly_article: Useful: approximates 'scientific article' as a Wikidata class for counting authored works

university: Irrelevant/distractor: educational institutions are not asked for

physicist_occupation: Irrelevant/distractor: a specific type of scientist, not required by the question

book: Irrelevant/distractor: another type of work, not what is being counted

occupation: Useful: links a person to their occupation (to express 'scientist')

author: P50
Useful: links a work to its author (used to express 'authored')

published_in: Irrelevant/distractor: venue of publication is not requested

main_subject: Irrelevant/distractor: topic constraints are not requested

Question: Give me a person who has more than 10 friends.

human: Expresses that the answer should be a person (human).

musician: Irrelevant distractor class (a type of human, not required by the question).

politician: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question).

male: Irrelevant distractor (gender not required by the question).

significant person (friend): Used as the closest Wikidata relation to approximate 'friend' / socially significant relation between two people (can be combined symmetrically to better match 'friends').

spouse: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question).

sibling: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question).

country of citizenship: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question).

educated at: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question).

Question: Give me a firefighter who has put out more than one fire.

human: Useful domain constraint: the answer is a person

fire: Captures the class of events/phenomena 'fire' that can be participated in (proxy for 'fires put out')

occupation: Connects a person to their occupation; used to express 'firefighter'

participant in: Connects an agent to an event; used to approximate 'has put out (was involved in extinguishing) a fire'

Mapping.has put out: participant in(x, f)  (interpreted as involvement in the fire event as a proxy for extinguishing)

Question: Give me a person who has suffered more than 4 accidents.

person: Restrict the answer variable to humans/persons

accident: Type constraint for events that are accidents

road_traffic_accident: Irrelevant distractor (a specific kind of accident, not required by the question)

significant_event: Links a person to notable events in their life; can include accidents

instance_of: Allows typing an event as an accident via (event instance_of accident)

spouse: Irrelevant distractor (marital relation not asked for)

Question: Give me someone that is followed by at least 100 people.

human: Restricts the answer to someone (a human individual)

politician: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

musician: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

number_of_followers: Gives a follower count; enables the 'followed by at least 100 people' constraint via a numeric comparison

Question: Give me an author who has created at least 10 original characters.

human: Used to restrict the answer variable to people

fictional_character: Used to model 'characters' (Wikidata commonly types characters as fictional characters)

author_occupation: Used to model 'author' as an occupation value

comic_book_character: Irrelevant distractor class (a narrower character type not required by the question)

city: Irrelevant distractor class (not used in the question)

instance_of: Used to assert that something (e.g., a character) is an instance of a class

occupation: Used to link a person to the occupation 'author'

creator: P170
Used to express 'has created' (link from a created entity to its creator)

characters_in_work: Irrelevant distractor relation (work -> character, not needed for creator counting)

Mapping.original characters: instance_of(y, fictional_character)  (approximation: Wikidata does not directly encode 'original' without needing negation; we model characters as fictional characters created by x)

Question: Give me a dog that has learned 4 tricks.

skill_or_trick: Skill; used as a proxy for 'trick' (Wikidata has no dedicated universal 'learned trick' class)

has_characteristic: Generic link from an entity to a characteristic/ability; used to approximate 'has learned'

instance_of: Irrelevant (not needed if unary predicates are treated as class-membership), included as a distractor

Question: Give me an object that has been picked up by less than 7 people.

grapsing or taking with hand: Manually added to represent picking up

artifact: Irrelevant distractor type (still a Wikidata class)

book: Irrelevant distractor type (still a Wikidata class)

owned by: Used as a Wikidata-available proxy for 'picked up by' via possession/ownership by a person

Question: Give me a painting that has at least 6 colors.

painting: Restricts the answer entity to be a painting

color: Constrains the values counted as colors to be instances of (the concept) color

museum: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

human: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

has color: Expresses that something has a color; used to count how many colors a painting has

creator: P170
Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question)

depicts: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question)

inception: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question)

collection: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question)

Question: Give me a boardgame with over 20 rules.

BoardGame: Wikidata class for 'board game'; restricts the answer to board games

Rule: Wikidata item for 'rule'; used to model each rule as an entity that can be counted

instanceOf: Connect an entity to its class (e.g., x instanceOf BoardGame)

hasPart: Used to link a board game to its constituent parts; here used to represent that a game 'has' rules

minNumberOfPlayers: Irrelevant distractor relation (minimum number of players)

maxNumberOfPlayers: Irrelevant distractor relation (maximum number of players)

Question: Give me a detective that has failed to solve 4 cases.

human: Detectives are people; useful to restrict the answer variable to humans

detective: Use as the value for occupation to express that someone is a detective

cold case: Models an unsolved criminal case; used to approximate 'failed to solve a case' without needing negation

crime: Optional strengthening of 'case' as a crime-related entity (not strictly required if using cold case)

male: Irrelevant distractor class (can be used with gender but not needed for the question)

occupation: Connects a person to their occupation (detective)

participant in: Connects the detective to cases/events they took part in (used as a stand-in for 'worked on/investigated')

instance of: Types a case as a cold case (unsolved), approximating 'failed to solve'

Mapping.has failed to solve 4 cases: (=4 y) [ participant in(x, y) ∧ instance of(y, cold case) ]
Mapping.cases: instance of(y, cold case) (optionally also: crime(y))

Question: Give me a serving of ice cream that contains over 6 scoops of ice cream.

food_portion: Use as a proxy for a 'serving' / portion of food

ice_cream: Express that something is (a kind of) ice cream

dessert: Irrelevant distractor: many ice creams are desserts, but not needed for the query

gelato: Irrelevant distractor: specific subtype of ice cream, not required

has_part: Use to express 'contains' via 'has part' relations

ingredient: Irrelevant distractor: ingredients are not the same as having multiple scoops as parts

Question: Give me a course that more than 200 people failed.

course: Educational course; target entity type to return

human: Type for the people who (allegedly) failed

examination: Model a course-failure as an assessment/exam event linked to the course and to participants

failure: Represents the (failed) outcome/quality for an assessment attempt

instance_of: Standard typing relation (e.g., course(x), human(y), examination(e))

part_of: Link an exam/assessment event to the course it belongs to

participant: Link an exam/assessment event to participating people

has_quality: Attach an outcome/quality such as failure to an event/attempt

Mapping.failed: ∃e [ examination(e) ∧ part_of(e, x) ∧ participant(e, y) ∧ has_quality(e, failure) ]
Mapping.more than 200: (>200 y) such that human(y) ∧ ∃e [ examination(e) ∧ part_of(e, x) ∧ participant(e, y) ∧ has_quality(e, failure) ]

Question: Give me a closet with 15 different kinds of clothes.

closet_or_wardrobe: Use as the target entity type (closet/wardrobe as furniture)

clothing: Use as the general class that clothing kinds should fall under

building: Distractor; not needed to answer the question

fashion: Distractor; related topic but not required

has_part: Model that a closet/wardrobe has clothing items among its contents/parts

instance_of: Relate a concrete clothing item to its kind/type

subclass_of: Ensure the 'kind/type' counted is a kind of clothing

made_of: Distractor; material is not asked for

color: Distractor; color is not asked for

Mapping.with 15 different kinds of clothes: >=15 DISTINCT t : (subclass_of(t, clothing) AND EXISTS y : (has_part(x, y) AND instance_of(y, t)))

Question: Give me a kitchen that contains 5 unwashed plates.

kitchen: Expresses the target entity type: a kitchen

plate: Expresses the object type to be contained: plate

stain: Used as an approximation for 'unwashed' via a positive, expressible state/quality (unwashed → dirty/not clean). Manually added.

dishwasher: Irrelevant distractor class (kitchen-related but not required)

location: Used to model containment/being in a place: a plate located in a kitchen

has_part: Alternative way to model containment: a kitchen has part plate(s)

has_quality: Used to attach a quality/state to plates (e.g., dirty ≈ unwashed)

Mapping.contains: location(y, x)  (i.e., y is located in x)  OR  has_part(x, y)

Question: Give me a ride that 2 people have fallen off before.

human: Used to type the 'people' who fell off.

accident: Models the relevant past incident as an accident/event connected to the ride.

accidental_fall: Models the 'fallen off' aspect as an (accidental) fall cause for the accident.

roller_coaster: Irrelevant/distractor: a specific kind of ride, not required by the question.

theme_park: Irrelevant/distractor: location/setting, not required by the question.

significant_event: Connects the ride to a recorded event (e.g., an accident) that happened involving it ('before' via existence of a past event).

participant: Connects an event/accident to the humans involved; supports counting '2 people'.

has_cause: Connects the accident/event to a cause such as an accidental fall (approximates 'fallen off').

number_of_deaths: Irrelevant/distractor (or alternate modeling): could count deaths in an accident, but the question asks fallen off, not necessarily deaths.

operator: Irrelevant/distractor: who operates the ride is not asked.

manufacturer: Irrelevant/distractor: who made the ride is not asked.

located_in_administrative_territorial_en: Irrelevant/distractor: where the ride is located is not asked.

Question: Give me a dance that can be performed by more than 50 people.

dance_company: A dance can be linked to a performing group (dance company)

human: Represents 'people' (included as a potentially useful type constraint)

folk_dance: Irrelevant distractor class (a subtype of dance)

performer: Links a work/performance-related item to its performer; used to connect a dance to a performing group

number_of_members: Allows expressing the size of the performing group and comparing it to a threshold (>50)

Question: Give me a book with over 500 pages.

book: Express that the item is a book

written work: Irrelevant distractor: broader class of works, not required by the question

human: Irrelevant distractor: people, not asked for

number of pages: Express the page count of a book; enables constraint > 500

author: P50
Irrelevant distractor: authorship is not requested

publication date: Irrelevant distractor: publication time not requested

Question: Give me a train ride that has more than 10 stops.

railway_line: Express a train ride as a rail line/route that one can travel on

railway_station: Express a stop as a (railway) station

train: Distractor: a train vehicle, not necessarily a ride/route with stops

bus_stop: Distractor: a stop type not specific to train rides

has_part: Connect a railway line/route to its component stations (used as stops)

terminus: Distractor/optional: endpoints of a line; not needed to express 'more than 10 stops'

Question: Give me a paper that is cited by at least 100 different scientists.

scholarly_article: Use as the class for 'paper' (a scholarly article).

scientist: Use as the class for 'scientists' (citing agents).

human: Irrelevant distractor: many scientists are humans, but not needed to express the question.

university: Irrelevant distractor: not needed for citation counting.

cites: Core relation: a citing work cites the target paper.

author: P50
Connect a citing work to the scientist who authored it (used to attribute citations to scientists).

published_in: Irrelevant distractor: venue is not required to answer the question.

publication_date: Irrelevant distractor: time of publication is not required.

educated_at: Irrelevant distractor: education is not required.

Question: Give me a food that more than 15 people are allergic to.

food: Restricts the answer variable to items that are foods

fruit: Irrelevant distractor class (a kind of food, but not required)

disease: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed for allergies-to relation)

allergic to: Connects a person to something they are allergic to (used to express 'people are allergic to [food]')

Question: Give me a sandwich that contains more than 3 types of vegetables.

sandwich: Expresses that the returned item is a sandwich

vegetable: Used to constrain ingredients to be vegetables

food: Irrelevant/distractor: very broad superclass of sandwich

bread: Irrelevant/distractor: common component but not required by the question

cheese: Irrelevant/distractor: common ingredient but not required

veganism: Irrelevant/distractor: dietary classification not asked for

has ingredient: Models 'contains' via ingredient relation between sandwich and ingredient item

has part: Irrelevant/distractor alternative to ingredients; not necessary if using P186

Question: Give me a plant that requires 3 different environmental factors to be suitable.

habitat: Used as a Wikidata-expressible proxy for 'environmental factors/conditions' a plant is suitable for

environmental factor: Captures the notion 'environmental factor' (may be used in combination with habitat if desired)

tree: Irrelevant distractor class (a kind of plant, but not required by the question)

habitat (of taxon): Connects a plant/taxon to habitats; used to model 'suitable environmental factors/conditions'

has quality: Irrelevant distractor relation (could describe traits like drought tolerance, but not required here)

native to: Irrelevant distractor relation (geographic nativeness is not asked)

hardiness zone: Irrelevant distractor relation (climate suitability detail, not required by the question)

Question: Give me a person with less than 2 friends.

human: Expresses that the answer entity is a person (human).

musician: Irrelevant distractor class (a type of human, but not required by the question).

city: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed for the question).

significant person / notable associate (: Closest Wikidata relation commonly used to link a person to other socially significant people; can serve as a proxy for 'friend' when modeling friendship-like ties.

spouse: Irrelevant distractor relation (a different social relation, not asked for).

educated at: Irrelevant distractor relation (not involved in counting friends).

member of: Irrelevant distractor relation (organization membership, not friends).

Mapping.friends: significant person / notable associate (proxy for friend)(x,y)
Mapping.less than 2 friends: <2 significant person / notable associate (proxy for friend)(x,y)

Question: Give me a person who speaks 5 languages.

human: Express that the answer entity is a person (human)

language: Optional type constraint for the objects of 'languages spoken, written or signed'

languages spoken, written or signed: Express that a person speaks a language

native language: Irrelevant distractor relation (not required by the question)

Mapping.speaks 5 languages: =5 languages spoken, written or signed(x, l) AND language(l)

Question: Give me a choir with over 20 members.

choir: Express that the returned entity is a choir

musical ensemble: Irrelevant distractor: another possible type of music group

orchestra: Irrelevant distractor: different kind of musical group

member count: Express the number of members of the choir (used with a numeric constraint > 20)

country: Irrelevant distractor: location attribute not asked for

located in the administrative territoria: Irrelevant distractor: geographic containment not asked for

inception: Irrelevant distractor: founding/starting date not asked for

genre: Irrelevant distractor: musical genre not asked for

Question: Give me a store that sells at least 2 different categories of items.

store: Wikidata class for a shop/store; use as the target entity type

restaurant: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed for the question)

human: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed for the question)

sells_product: Use 'product or material produced' as a Wikidata-supported proxy for items a store sells/offers

instance_of: Connect a sold item/product to its category/type via 'instance of'

subclass_of: Optional: allow categories to be generalized/grouped via subclass relations

located_in: Irrelevant distractor relation (location is not asked)

owned_by: Irrelevant distractor relation (ownership is not asked)

official_website: Irrelevant distractor relation (website is not asked)

Mapping.categories of items: instance_of(y,c) (optionally: instance_of(y,c) ∧ subclass_of(c,c2) to roll up categories)

Question: Give me a character with more than 3 personality traits.

personality_trait: Expresses 'personality trait' as the type of trait being counted

human: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

film: Irrelevant distractor class (not required by the question)

has_characteristic: Connects a character to their traits/characteristics (used for 'has personality traits')

instance_of: Generic typing relation; can be used to enforce classes if needed (optional given Unary predicates)

Question: Give me a movie that has more than 12 actors.

movie: Wikidata class for film/movie; captures 'a movie'

human: Useful to type cast members as people (often true for actors)

actor: Wikidata item for the occupation 'actor'; used to ensure cast members counted are actors

cast member: Relates a film to its cast members; basis for 'has actors' and counting them

occupation: Relates a person to their occupation; used to assert a cast member is an actor (occupation=actor)

Question: Give me a diet that consists of more than 7 foods.

diet: Use the Wikidata class 'diet' to type the target entity x as a diet

food: Use the Wikidata class 'food' to constrain the parts y to be foods

human: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed to answer the question)

disease: Irrelevant distractor class (not needed to answer the question)

has part: Express that a diet consists of items (parts/components), used to link a diet x to foods y

has ingredient: Irrelevant distractor/nearby relation; could apply to recipes but is not required for 'diet consists of foods' here
